cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Confess First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to confess or incriminate themselves before you reveal anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Before we plan Mum's apology dinner, why did she spend her birthday outside the restaurant?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I forgot the booking. What happened to her present?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Did you forget, or assume I'd book it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I assumed you'd do it. Now your turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even after telling Mum it was confirmed? Give me that bit, then you get the present.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 takes decision power, A3 defers B present question, and A5 sets a further confession condition before granting the requested topic.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 forgetting claim is tested by A3 against assumption; B4 admits assumption and demands a turn, causing A5 to ask about prior assurance.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 seek reciprocity while owning booking responsibility, giving B a credible family stake rather than passive guilt.

heightening.evidence: B4 admission does not end A control: A5 probes the more incriminating confirmed-booking claim before disclosure.

specificity.evidence: A1 apology dinner and Mum outside a restaurant establish the family mishap; B2 introduces the separate present question.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 give-me-that-bit condition is concise and earned by B4 now-your-turn demand, though present wording has mild ambiguity.
